title: SDK Integration Contract and Bundle Validator Playbook (2025)
summary: Playbook for validating SDK integration contracts and packaging distribution bundles before rollout. Covers the checks, dx-validate CLI flows, common failures with canonical fixes, and a simple gating policy for PR and release pipelines.
body:
Overview

This playbook covers the SDK integration contract checks and the bundle validator that run in DX CI and release pipelines. The aim is to catch integration regressions (API surface changes, telemetry gaps, schema drift) before SDK packages reach registries or customers. The validator is kept lightweight so it fits in PR checks as well as nightly runs.

When to use

- Any PR touching the public SDK surface, request/response shapes, telemetry events, or packaged assets (wheel/tarball/npm).
- Before cutting a release candidate (rc) and before publishing to internal registries.
- For customer-specific integration checks during Dedicated/Private handoffs.

Definitions

- Integration Contract: stable request/response JSON schemas, endpoint names and client method signatures, error-code set, and telemetry event list.
- Bundle: the packaged distribution (pip wheel, npm package) plus README, changelog, schemas, sample prompts, and telemetry spec.
- Validator: CLI running static and dynamic checks on a candidate bundle against a baseline contract.

Roles & Ownership

- SDK Owner (default: dx-sdk team): maintains contract files, fixes failures, interprets validator output.
- DX Validator Maintainer (default: devx-infra): owns validator code, rule set, and baseline contracts.
- Release Manager: approves release once the validator is green.

Gating policy

- PR gate (fast): lint, public API diff, required files. Required before merge.
- RC gate (full): end-to-end example against staging runtime, telemetry sample verification, packaging verification. Required before publishing.

PR checklist

1. public_api.yaml present and valid
2. schema/request/ and schema/response/ changed only with an ADR or migration notes
3. telemetry-events.yaml updated for trackable changes
4. sample-usage.* updated and run in the CI smoke test
5. package artifact builds and its sha256 checksum is verified

Validator commands

# Install
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/dx-validator.git@main

# Full validation of a wheel
dx-validate bundle --bundle dist/redwood_sdk-1.1.0-py3-none-any.whl --baseline contracts/baseline-2025-10.json --staging-url https://staging.api.redwood.ai

# Fast PR checks
dx-validate quick --src ./src/redwood_sdk --public-api public_api.yaml --telemetry telemetry-events.yaml

What the validator checks

Static (fast)
- public API diff (added/removed/changed methods and parameters)
- presence and lint of public_api.yaml, telemetry-events.yaml, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE
- packaging manifest sanity (pyproject.toml / package.json, included files)

Schema (medium)
- request/response schema compatibility with the baseline (additive changes only unless flagged)
- no error/status codes removed that the baseline uses
- example payloads validate against declared schemas

Dynamic (slow)
- smoke call against staging runtime with output shape validation
- telemetry emission: sample calls must produce the expected events within 60s window at the telemetry-proxy test endpoint
- integration example scripts exit 0

Failure modes and canonical fixes

1) Public API removed or renamed
Fix: revert or add a compatibility shim; write an ADR and migration notes for intentional breaks and bump the major version.

2) Schema drift breaking customers
Fix: restore required fields or ship a compatibility adapter; update schema migration notes and add an eval test for the edge case.

3) Telemetry missing or incomplete
Fix: make sure instrumentation fires; check flush behavior in async clients; add tests asserting event attributes.

4) Packaging missing files (README, LICENSE, sample prompts)
Fix: update the pyproject/package.json include list and add a CI gate validating artifact contents and checksum.

Snippets

- Compatibility shim (Python):
from typing import Any

def summarize(text: Any, model: Any = None):
    # accept old and new call styles
    return _impl_summarize(str(text), model=model)

- Telemetry flush (async client):
await client.emit_event("generation_request", {"model": model_name})
await client.flush(timeout_seconds=5)

CI YAML excerpt

steps:
  - run: python -m pip wheel . -w dist/
  - run: dx-validate bundle --bundle dist/*.whl --baseline contracts/baseline-2025-10.json

E2E smoke test

1. Start telemetry-proxy locally (docker run -p 9001:9001 redwood/telemetry-proxy:test)
2. Install the candidate wheel in a virtualenv
3. Run sample-usage/smoke_invoke.py: create a client, call generate(sample_prompt), assert non-empty text, poll telemetry-proxy for the event.

Validator targets

- PR quick-check median: < 90s
- RC full-check median: < 900s
- False positive rate: < 2% per quarter
- At least 3 canonical flows per SDK (generation, embeddings, health-check)

Telemetry expectations

- Events: generation.request, generation.response, sdk.install, sdk.error
- generation.request fields: client_id, request_id, model, prompt_length, timestamp
- generation.response fields: request_id, latency_ms, tokens_generated, status

Rollout guidance

- Canary: publish the RC to the internal channel and run the RC full-check against a reserved staging project for 48 hours, watching SDK error rate, telemetry missing-field rate, and runtime latency delta.
- Gradual: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 72 hours if metrics hold.

Post-release triage

1. Reproduce with dx-validate reproduce --bundle <bundle> --baseline <baseline>
2. Collect telemetry-proxy and staging runtime logs with the failing request_id
3. Patch, rerun the RC full-check, and promote through canary when green

FAQ

Q: Who updates baseline contracts?
A: DX Validator Maintainers, after an authorized platform/API change. SDK teams notify them in #dx-validator and attach ADRs for breaking changes.

Q: Can a check be disabled for a hotfix?
A: Only the Release Manager may disable a check temporarily. Record the exception in the PR, re-enable within three business days, and list it in the release notes.

Appendix: public_api.yaml example

methods:
  - name: generate
    description: "Synchronous text generation method"
    params:
      - name: prompt
        type: string
        required: true
      - name: model
        type: string
        required: false
    returns:
      type: object
      schema: response/generate.json

Appendix: telemetry-events.yaml example

events:
  - name: generation.request
    required_fields: [client_id, request_id, model, prompt_length, timestamp]
  - name: generation.response
    required_fields: [request_id, latency_ms, tokens_generated, status]
